headline: Global RevPAR growth prompts a raised full-year outlook
summary_short: Marriott reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $7.07 billion, up 4.8% y/y, with GAAP diluted EPS of $2.90 (+4.3% y/y) and net income roughly flat at $766 million, as worldwide RevPAR rose 3.4%.
summary_long: Revenue rose 4.8% y/y to $7.07 billion, driven by 14% growth in franchise and base management fees ($1.37B) on higher co-branded card fees, rooms growth, and RevPAR (worldwide +3.4%; U.S. & Canada +5.0%; international -0.5% on Middle East headwinds). Reported operating income ($1.229B) and net income ($766M, $2.90/diluted share) were roughly flat y/y, held back by a $27M litigation accrual and a $68M hotel-sale impairment; Adjusted net income rose 16% to $844M ($3.19/share) and Adjusted EBITDA rose 13% to $1.592B. Total debt rose to $16.9B from $16.2B at year-end 2025. Marriott raised full-year 2026 RevPAR growth guidance to 3.0%-3.5% and guided Adjusted diluted EPS to $11.64-$11.81.
confidence_notes: The resolver's shard KPI 'long_term_debt_usd_m' ($23M) does not represent Marriott's total debt -- it appears to capture a narrow debt sub-category (likely capital-lease-type obligations) rather than the ~$16.9B total debt the release itself discloses; this summary uses the release's own total-debt figure in the narrative rather than the shard field. Shareholders' equity is negative, a long-standing feature of Marriott's capital structure driven by cumulative share buybacks, not a solvency signal.

drivers.explanation: Franchise and base management fee growth (+14% y/y) was driven by higher co-branded credit card fees, rooms growth, and higher RevPAR.
GAAP net income was held roughly flat by a $27M property-related litigation accrual and a $68M impairment on a U.S. & Canada hotel sale, both excluded from Adjusted results.
Full-year RevPAR growth guidance was raised to 3.0%-3.5% citing Q2 outperformance and continued broad-based demand.
